questions.question: When should you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you move left or right. Signal when entering traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on major highways?

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: On highways, stay alert and be ready for unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis—do not look at one spot for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: When should you turn on your headlights?

options.text: When stopped at a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Turn on headlights one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when windshield wipers are on due to rain or snow, or when visibility is less than 500 feet.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful approaching them from behind. On hills with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if other drivers are acting angry?
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, distance yourself from them both physically and mentally. Avoid eye contact and hand gestures. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you can safely do to stay out of danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead is showing red.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead is showing green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person involved with a traffic study.

questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog—they are blind and need your help.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep your tires properly filled with air.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases this risk.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Watches what other drivers are doing.
Travels at the same speed always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches for what other drivers are doing and expects problems before they happen. This helps avoid accidents even when other drivers are distracted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is coming. Enter it slowly and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to arrange a ride with a friend who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. Your body eliminates about one drink per hour.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you are not feeling tired.

questions.question: It is important to slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, around pedestrians, when driving hazards are present, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
The road you are on meets a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road you are on meets a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that your road meets a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work at all times when driving.

questions.question: Two solid white lines across a traffic lane show where a crosswalk is. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians in crosswalks have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show pedestrians where to safely cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: When you see a steady green light, let pedestrians and remaining vehicles pass first. You can continue, but be ready to slow down and stop if the light changes before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow normal road laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Always obey flaggers in construction zones. Slow down and use caution when they direct you to do so. Failing to obey is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully and watch for hazards.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival is very unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous. Other drivers may become impatient and make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move to clear the path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to clear the path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, clear a path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, you should use ____ to indicate that you are turning.
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show other drivers which way you plan to turn.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly through turns and curves. Slow down more than you normally would in these conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following must you obey over the other three?
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions override signs, signals, and road markings. Traffic officers who can direct traffic include police officers, fire police, work zone flag persons, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive through and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first. Let it pass safely before you proceed.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
Rain is more likely at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: Your vision is limited at night. Always use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear before entering.

questions.explanation: Signal early before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: Check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position, including when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped, orange with black letters, and warn that workers are on or near the highway.
